20261122-chemistry-e2-2.material: Why water and cooking oil dey separate again into two layers after small time, even if you put dem inside one bottle and shake am well well?
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.thinking.0: Why water and cooking oil dey
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.prompt: Why water and cooking oil dey separate again into two layers after small time, even if you put dem inside one bottle and shake am well well?
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.explain: Water na polar molecule and cooking oil na non-polar molecule, so dem no dey mix, and di density of cooking oil (about 0.92 g/cm³) small pass water (1.0 g/cm³), so e dey float to di top layer.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.hint.0: Water dey polar and oil dey non-polar, so dem no dey dissolve each other.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.hint.1: Oil lighter than water (less dense) so e dey float for top.
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o0: Because cooking oil no dey mix with water and e lighter (less dense) than water so e dey float for top
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o1: Because cooking oil dey absorb di water
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o2: Because di water warm pass di cooking oil
20261122-chemistry-e2-2.s.s1.o.o3: Because di cooking oil don turn solid
